s: The ____ dynasty ruled over Andhra country from 12th to 13th centuries.
x: The Kakatiyas ruled the Andhra country in the 12th-13th centuries (independent from 1163 to 1323) from Hanumakonda and Orugallu. The Western Chalukyas and Cholas were earlier, the Yadavas ruled Maharashtra.

s: One of the major dynasties that ruled over Andhra
x: All four ruled parts of Andhra, so the question is loose; the intended answer is the Satavahanas, the first and greatest major dynasty of Andhra (the Kakatiyas were the second to unite all Telugu lands). Keyed as printed.

s: The Dynasty which had given ultimate design to Andhra culture and civilisation was
x: The Kakatiyas united the whole Andhra region and 'gave a comprehensive form to Andhraism' - Telugu identity, Orugallu as Andhranagari - so they gave Andhra culture its final shape. The Satavahanas, Pallavas and Chalukyas came earlier.

s: Which of the following clans the first rulers of Jains are believed?
x: The Kakatiyas were initially Jains and later embraced Shaivism, so they are the clan whose first rulers were Jains. The Satavahanas were Brahmanical, the Guptas Vaishnava, the Reddis Shaiva.

s: Bayyaram inscription tells about whose history?
x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of Mailamba (Ganapatideva's sister) gives the genealogy of the early Kakatiyas from Venna Bhupati. It has nothing to do with the Reddis, Badami Chalukyas or Satavahanas.

s: Who was the Raja Guru of Ganapatideva?
x: Visvesvara Sivacharya (Visvesvara Siva), head of the Golaki Matha, was Ganapatideva's raja guru. Vidyanatha was Prataparudra's court poet; Mallikarjuna Pandita and Sripati Pandita were Saiva teachers, not his guru.

s: Kakatiyas were feudatories of which Andhra dynasty?
x: The Kakatiyas first appear as Rashtrakuta vassals (Gundaya 'Rashtrakuta', Garuda emblem) and later served the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas only issued the Magallu grant that first mentions them; they were never Kakatiya overlords.

s: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before establishing their independent kingdom?
x: The early Kakatiyas were feudatories of the Rashtrakutas (Magallu: Gundaya 'Rashtrakuta'), then of the Kalyani Chalukyas. They were never vassals of the Yadavas, the Eastern Chalukyas or the Hoysalas.

s: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before taking over the kingdom?
x: The Kakatiyas were originally feudatories of the Rashtrakutas (Garuda emblem) and later of the Kalyani Chalukyas (Varaha emblem). The Yadavas, Vengi Chalukyas and Hoysalas were neighbours or rivals.

s: Kakatiyas were subordinates of which dynasty in Andhra
x: The Kakatiyas were first subordinates of the Rashtrakutas, and only later of the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas only issued the Magallu grant that first mentions them.

s: According to which of the following was 'Veena' the founder of the Kakatiya family?
x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of Mailamba traces the Kakatiyas from Venna (Venna Bhupati) as the first of the line. The Kazipet inscription names Beta I; Junagarh and Vijayawada are unrelated.

s: Who were the kings who had the title 'Mahamandaleswara'?
x: The Kakatiya rulers, as feudatories of the Kalyani Chalukyas, bore the title Mahamandaleswara (Beta II took it). It is a feudatory title, so the overlord Chalukya and Rashtrakuta kings did not use it as their style.

s: Who is the Guru of Ganapati Deva?
x: Visvesvara Sivacharya (Visvesvara Sambhu) of the Golaki Matha was Ganapatideva's guru. Vidyanatha was Prataparudra's court poet, Palkuriki Somanatha a Virasaiva poet.

s: Religious teacher of Ganapati Deva?
x: Visvesvara Sivacharya was Ganapatideva's guru. Rameswara Pandita was Beta II's guru and Dhruveshwara Pandita Mahadeva's.

s: According to which inscription was Beta Raja-I the first Kakatiya king?
x: The Kazipet (Dargah) inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I and names him the first Kakatiya king. Junagadh is Rudradaman's record, Gantasala and Amaravati are Buddhist sites.

s: According to which inscription was Beta Raja I the first Kakatiya king?
x: The Kazipet (Dargah) inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I and names him the first Kakatiya ruler. The other inscriptions are not linked to the Kakatiya genealogy.

s: Betha Raj-I was the first Kakatiya king according to the
x: The Kazipet Dargah inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I, naming him the first Kakatiya ruler. Junagadh, Ghantasala and Amaravati are unrelated.

s: For the first time, in which inscription were the Kakatiyas mentioned?
x: The Kakatiyas are first mentioned in the Magallu inscription (c. 950-956) of the Eastern Chalukya king Danarnava, through Kakatiya Gundyana. Bayyaram (13th c.) is later; Polavaram and Pillalamarri are unrelated.

s: Which inscription mentioned about Kakatiyas for the first time
x: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava (c. 950-956) is the first mention of the Kakatiyas (Gundyana). Bayyaram is a later genealogy.

s:

How many of the above dynasties established their kingdoms in early eighth century AD?
